summary.text: A 25-year-old man arrived at the emergency department of a university hospital in Beirut with agitation, disorganized behavior, confusion and dysarthria. Earlier outpatient MRI and EEG were normal, and escitalopram had brought no improvement. He was started on risperidone, diazepam and chlorpromazine and admitted to the psychiatric ward after a routine blood test. Over Days 1-6 he worsened, with perioral dyskinesia, disorientation and hallucinations.

From Day 8 to Day 12 he gradually lost consciousness, then developed catatonic signs until Day 14 and received one ECT session without improvement. A second EEG on Day 15 showed moderate diffuse cerebral dysfunction. He had a first tonic-clonic seizure, pneumonia was diagnosed on Day 16, and a lumbar puncture showed an increased CSF IgG index. A third EEG on Day 17 showed an extreme delta brush aspect, and a testicular ultrasound was normal.

Methylprednisolone and valproic acid were started on Day 17, after which he became more alert; a second generalized seizure occurred on Day 18. Plasmapheresis (five sessions, Days 23-32) was added for incomplete corticosteroid response, and carbamazepine, clonazepam and levetiracetam were added for persistent seizures. Nosocomial pneumonia led to ICU care from Day 35 to Day 43, with intubation and extubation without complications.

He left the hospital on Day 45, alert, oriented and cooperative, taking antiepileptics and prednisone. Five days after discharge the CSF NMDA antibody titer was positive, confirming anti-NMDAR encephalitis; outside tests were unremarkable. An EEG 3 months after discharge was normal. Recovery progressed well, with mild memory deficits and a depressive episode treated with an SSRI; rituximab was considered in case of relapse.
